user.title: Add discrete statistics
user.description: Records how long this entity spends in each state, and how often it changes, as long-term statistics kept independently of the recorder's purge window.

data_description.entity_id: The binary or enum entity to track. It cannot be changed later, because it determines the statistic IDs.
data_description.name: Shown on charts. Defaults to the entity's own name.
data_description.default: Time in an ignored state is credited to the previous recorded state - it never creates a gap, and it does not count as a transition. The two choices that mention a minimum duration need it set below.
data_description.blank: Some entities report a state with no letters or digits at all - empty, or punctuation. That has no name to record under, so this says what becomes of it. Type any state name to record it as that instead.
data_description.min_duration: Used only by the choices that mention it. A state the entity leaves again sooner than this is not recorded: the previous state carries on as though it had never been left, and no transition is counted. At most one hour.

abort.already_configured: This entity already has discrete statistics.
abort.yaml_configured: This entity is configured in configuration.yaml. Edit it there, or remove it from YAML first.

error.blank_record: A blank state has no name to record it under. Choose Ignore, or type a state name to record it as.
error.blank_unusable: That has no letters or digits either, so it cannot name a statistic. Choose Ignore, or type a state name.
error.continuous_state: That entity reports a continuous measurement. Discrete Statistics tracks entities with a fixed set of states, such as on/off or a list of modes.
error.min_duration_required: That choice needs a minimum duration longer than zero.

data_description.name: Shown on charts. Leave blank to follow the entity’s own name, currently “{default_name}”.
data_description.default: Time in an ignored state is credited to the previous recorded state - it never creates a gap, and it does not count as a transition. The two choices that mention a minimum duration need it set below. Changing this recompiles the entity's whole history.
data_description.blank: Some entities report a state with no letters or digits at all - empty, or punctuation. That has no name to record under, so this says what becomes of it. Type any state name to record it as that instead.
data_description.min_duration: Used only by the choices that mention it. A state the entity leaves again sooner than this is not recorded: the previous state carries on as though it had never been left, and no transition is counted. At most one hour.

error.blank_record: A blank state has no name to record it under. Choose Ignore, or type a state name to record it as.
error.blank_unusable: That has no letters or digits either, so it cannot name a statistic. Choose Ignore, or type a state name.
error.min_duration_required: That choice needs a minimum duration longer than zero.

options.record: Record every state, including unavailable and unknown
options.record_known: Record known states, ignoring unavailable and unknown
options.ignore_short_unknown: Record known states, and unavailable and unknown only when they last a minimum duration
options.ignore_short: Record every state only when it lasts a minimum duration, including unavailable and unknown

options.unknown: Record as unknown (ignored unless you record unknown states)
options.ignore: Ignore - carry the previous state forward

yaml_clash.title: Duplicate configuration for {entity_id}
yaml_clash.description: {entity_id} is configured both in configuration.yaml and as a helper. The YAML configuration is being used and the helper has been disabled, because two configurations write conflicting values to the same statistics. Remove one of them.
